records.source: הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Give thanks to YHWH, for [he is] good; for forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever.

L.1: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever.

R.1: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good! His faithful love lasts forever.

decisions.choice: Psalm 118: a song of thanks for the festival procession
decisions.reason: The last psalm of the Hallel (113-118) is a liturgy: a call to give thanks (verses 1-4), the king's or worshiper's story of rescue (5-18), the entry through the temple gates (19-21), the people's and priests' response (22-27), and a closing thanks (28-29). Several voices seem to speak in turn.

decisions.choice: the refrain of thanksgiving
decisions.reason: "Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his loyal love is forever" was the song of the temple singers (1 Chronicles 16:34; Ezra 3:11) and opens Psalms 106, 107 and 136. Verse 29 repeats it to close the psalm.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: for his loyal love lasts forever (B); His faithful love lasts forever (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain (ki le'olam chasdo) has the same English each time it occurs at each level, here and in verses 2-4 and 29, as in Psalm 136.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.heading: The stone the builders cast aside

records.source: יֹֽאמַר־נָ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Let Israel say now: For forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: Let Israel say it now: "His loyal love lasts forever."

L.2: Let Israel say now: "For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever."

R.2: Let the people of Israel say, "His faithful love lasts forever!"

decisions.choice: Israel, the house of Aaron, those who fear the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 115:9-11, three groups are called in turn: all Israel, the priests, and all who fear the LORD. Each answers with the refrain.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 118:1.

decisions.choice: the words to be said
decisions.reason: The joining word (ki) introduces what they are to say; it is shown as a quotation.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: יֹֽאמְרוּ־נָ֥א בֵֽית־אַהֲרֹ֑ן כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Let [the] house of Aaron say now: For forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: Let the house of Aaron say it now: "His loyal love lasts forever."

L.3: Let the house of Aaron say now: "For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever."

R.3: Let the priests of Aaron's family say, "His faithful love lasts forever!"

decisions.choice: house of Aaron: the priests
loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 118:1.

decisions.choice: the priests of Aaron's family
faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: יֹֽאמְרוּ־נָ֭א יִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Let [those who] fear YHWH say now: For forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: Let those who fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say it now: "His loyal love lasts forever."

L.4: Let those who fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say now: "For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever."

R.4: Let all who fear and honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say, "His faithful love lasts forever!"

decisions.choice: those who fear the LORD
loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 118:1.

decisions.choice: fear and honor
decisions.reason: As in 111:5.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: מִֽן־הַ֭מֵּצַ֥ר קָרָ֣אתִי יָּ֑הּ עָנָ֖נִי בַמֶּרְחָ֣ב יָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: From the distress I called Yah; Yah answered me in the broad place.
pieces: When I was hemmed in I called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} answered me by bringing me out into open space.

L.5: Out of the narrow place I called [to] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} answered me in the broad place.

R.5: I was in great trouble, and I called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} answered and brought me out to a safe, open place.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: the narrow place ... the broad place: distress and freedom
decisions.reason: Distress (metsar) is being squeezed in a tight place; rescue is room to move (merchav), as in 4:2 and 18:20.

decisions.choice: answered me in the broad place: answered and set me free
decisions.reason: The phrase is short: the LORD answered by bringing him out into the open.

decisions.choice: bringing me out into (B); set me in (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the movement the Hebrew implies (m3).

records.source: יְהוָ֣ה לִ֭י לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לִ֣י אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: YHWH [is] for me; not I will fear; what can do to me a human?
pieces: With {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for me, I have no fear. What can any human being do to me?

L.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] for me; I will not fear; what can a human do to me?

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is on my side, so I am not afraid. What can anyone do to me?

decisions.choice: quoted in Hebrews 13:6
decisions.reason: Hebrews quotes this verse, from the ancient Greek translation, as the confident answer of those whom God will never leave. 56:5 and 56:12 say the same.

decisions.choice: for me: on my side
decisions.reason: "The LORD is for me" means he takes my part (56:10).

records.source: יְהוָ֣ה לִ֭י בְּעֹזְרָ֑י וַ֝אֲנִ֗י אֶרְאֶ֥ה בְשֹׂנְאָֽי׃
records.gloss: YHWH [is] for me among my helpers, and I, I will look on those who hate me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is with me as my helper, and I will see the downfall of those who hate me.

L.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] for me among my helpers, and I will look on those who hate me.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is on my side to help me. I will see my enemies defeated.

decisions.choice: among my helpers: as my helper
alternatives: is among those who help me
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that the LORD is one of his helpers, but more likely it means that he is the helper, the one who counts (54:6).

decisions.choice: look on those who hate me: see their defeat
decisions.reason: As in 112:8.

decisions.choice: see my enemies defeated
alternatives: look on those who hate me
decisions.reason: As in 112:8.

records.source: ט֗וֹב לַחֲס֥וֹת בַּיהוָ֑ה מִ֝בְּטֹ֗חַ בָּאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Better to take refuge in YHWH than to trust in humankind.
pieces: It is better to make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your refuge than to rely on human beings.

L.8: [It is] better to take refuge in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} than to trust in humankind.

R.8: It is better to run to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for safety than to depend on people.

decisions.choice: take refuge: run to for shelter
decisions.reason: As in 2:12 and 7:2, the verb (chasah) is to seek shelter in someone.

decisions.choice: do not trust in mortals
decisions.reason: 146:3 and Jeremiah 17:5-7 say the same: human help fails, the LORD does not.

decisions.choice: make the LORD your refuge (B); run to the LORD for safety (R)
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms.

records.source: ט֗וֹב לַחֲס֥וֹת בַּיהוָ֑ה מִ֝בְּטֹ֗חַ בִּנְדִיבִֽים׃
records.gloss: Better to take refuge in YHWH than to trust in nobles.
pieces: It is better to make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your refuge than to rely on princes.

L.9: [It is] better to take refuge in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} than to trust in nobles.

R.9: It is better to run to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for safety than to depend on powerful leaders.

decisions.choice: nobles: people of power
decisions.reason: As in 113:8; even the powerful are only human (146:3).

decisions.choice: make the LORD your refuge (B); run to the LORD for safety (R)
decisions.reason: As in 118:8.

records.source: כָּל־גּוֹיִ֥ם סְבָב֑וּנִי בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם׃
records.gloss: All nations surrounded me; in [the] name of YHWH indeed I cut them off.
pieces: All the nations closed in around me; in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I drove them back.

L.10: All nations surrounded me; in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I surely cut them off.

R.10: Enemy nations came at me from every side, but with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s power I fought them off.

decisions.choice: all nations surrounded me: the king in battle
decisions.reason: The speaker is surrounded by nations, which suits a king leading Israel in war, or Israel itself speaking as one person.

decisions.choice: in the name of the LORD: by his authority and power
decisions.reason: To fight in the LORD's name is to fight relying on him and his power (20:6, 8; 1 Samuel 17:45).

decisions.choice: I cut them off: I drove them away
decisions.reason: The verb ('amilam, from mul) is rare in this sense; the same root means to cut, and it may mean "cut off" or "ward off". Either way, the enemies are beaten back "in the name of the LORD".

decisions.choice: with the LORD's power
alternatives: in the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what fighting in the LORD's name means (the meaning decision on the phrase).

records.source: סַבּ֥וּנִי גַם־סְבָב֑וּנִי בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם׃
records.gloss: They surrounded me, also they surrounded me; in [the] name of YHWH indeed I cut them off.
pieces: They closed in around me, yes, they closed in on every side; in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I drove them back.

L.11: They surrounded me, yes, they surrounded me; in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I surely cut them off.

R.11: They were all around me, yes, all around me, but with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s power I fought them off.

decisions.choice: the repetition: being hemmed in on every side
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated, as is the line about the name of the LORD, to build the feeling of danger and of the victory (verses 10-12).

decisions.choice: in the name of the LORD: by his authority and power
I cut them off: I drove them away
with the LORD's power
alternatives: in the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what fighting in the LORD's name means (the meaning decision on the phrase).

records.source: סַבּ֤וּנִי כִדְבוֹרִ֗ים דֹּ֭עֲכוּ כְּאֵ֣שׁ קוֹצִ֑ים בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם׃
records.gloss: They surrounded me like bees; they were extinguished like a fire of thorns; in [the] name of YHWH indeed I cut them off.
pieces: They came at me like a swarm of bees, but they burned out like a fire in thornbushes; in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I drove them back.

L.12: They surrounded me like bees; they were extinguished like a fire of thorns; in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I surely cut them off.

R.12: They attacked me like a swarm of bees. But they were gone as quickly as a fire in dry thorns burns out. With {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s power I fought them off.

decisions.choice: like bees: a swarm that stings from every side
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 1:44 pictures the Amorites chasing Israel "as bees do".

decisions.choice: they were put out: as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text says the enemies "were extinguished" like a thorn fire, which flares up and quickly dies. The ancient Greek translation has "they blazed up", which goes with the fierceness of the attack. The renderings follow the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: in the name of the LORD: by his authority and power
I cut them off: I drove them away
with the LORD's power
alternatives: in the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what fighting in the LORD's name means (the meaning decision on the phrase).

records.source: דַּחֹ֣ה דְחִיתַ֣נִי לִנְפֹּ֑ל וַ֖יהוָ֣ה עֲזָרָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Pushing you pushed me to fall, but YHWH helped me.
pieces: You shoved me hard to make me fall, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to my help.

L.13: You pushed me hard so that I would fall, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} helped me.

R.13: My enemy pushed me hard to knock me down, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} helped me.

decisions.choice: you: the enemy, addressed directly
decisions.reason: The speaker suddenly turns to the enemy, now spoken of as one. The doubled verb stresses the force of the push.

decisions.choice: you pushed me: as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation and other early versions read "I was pushed". The renderings follow the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: My enemy
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed, to avoid confusion with God (m1).

records.source: עָזִּ֣י וְזִמְרָ֣ת יָ֑הּ וַֽיְהִי־לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: My strength and song [is] Yah, and he has become for me salvation.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} is my strength and the theme of my song; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has come to my rescue.

L.14: My strength and song [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has become my salvation.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} makes me strong and gives me a song to sing. He has saved me.

decisions.choice: the Song of the Sea: Exodus 15:2
decisions.reason: The line is word for word from the song Moses and Israel sang after crossing the sea (Exodus 15:2), also taken up in Isaiah 12:2. The rescue is celebrated as a new exodus.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: song: a song of praise, or might
decisions.reason: The word (zimrat) usually means song; some take it here, as in Exodus 15:2, as "strength" or "protection", a second word for the same thing.

decisions.choice: come to my rescue (B); saved me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means that he has become salvation for me.

records.source: ק֤וֹל׀רִנָּ֬ה וִֽישׁוּעָ֗ה בְּאָהֳלֵ֥י צַדִּיקִ֑ים יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: [The] sound of [a] glad shout and salvation [is] in [the] tents of [the] righteous: [The] right hand of YHWH does valiantly.
pieces: The tents of the righteous ring with glad shouts of rescue: "The right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} acts with power!

L.15: The sound of a glad shout and of salvation [is] in the tents of the righteous: "The right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does valiantly!

R.15: People who do what is right are shouting for joy in their tents because they have been saved: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power!

decisions.choice: the shout quoted through verse 16
decisions.reason: The words after the colon are the shout heard in the tents; the quotation runs to the end of verse 16.

decisions.choice: the right hand of the LORD: his power in action
decisions.reason: The right hand is the hand of strength; the words echo Exodus 15:6, 12.

decisions.choice: does valiantly: acts with might
decisions.reason: The phrase ('oseh chayil) is to show strength, as a warrior does (60:14).

decisions.choice: the LORD has used his great power
alternatives: the right hand of the LORD does valiantly
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

records.source: יְמִ֣ין יְ֭הוָה רוֹמֵמָ֑ה יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: [The] right hand of YHWH [is] lifted high; [the] right hand of YHWH does valiantly.
pieces: The right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is raised in triumph; the right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} acts with power!"

L.16: The right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] lifted high; the right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does valiantly!"

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand to win the victory. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power!"

decisions.choice: lifted high: raised in victory
decisions.reason: The form (romemah) may mean that the LORD's hand is raised high in victory, or that it lifts up the one it saves.

decisions.choice: the right hand of the LORD
has raised his hand to win the victory
alternatives: the right hand of the LORD is lifted high
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.source: לֹֽא אָמ֥וּת כִּי־אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר מַֽעֲשֵׂ֥י יָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Not I will die, but I will live, and I will recount [the] deeds of Yah.
pieces: I am not going to die; I will live and tell what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} has done.

L.17: I will not die, but I will live, and I will recount the deeds of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.

R.17: I will not die! I will live and tell everyone what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} has done.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: recount: tell in order, declare
decisions.reason: The verb (siper) is to tell over, to rehearse a story (9:2; 78:4).

records.source: יַסֹּ֣ר יִסְּרַ֣נִּי יָּ֑הּ וְ֝לַמָּ֗וֶת לֹ֣א נְתָנָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Disciplining Yah has disciplined me, but to the death not he has given me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} disciplined me hard, yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not let death take me.

L.18: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} has severely disciplined me, but to death {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has not given me over.

R.18: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} corrected me very strictly, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not let me die.

decisions.choice: disciplined: corrected, as a father corrects
decisions.reason: The verb (yissar) is to discipline or train, as a father does a son (94:12; Proverbs 3:11-12). The doubled verb stresses how hard it was.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

records.source: פִּתְחוּ־לִ֥י שַׁעֲרֵי־צֶ֑דֶק אָֽבֹא־בָ֝ם אוֹדֶ֥ה יָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Open to me [the] gates of righteousness; I will go in through them; I will give thanks to Yah.
pieces: Open the gates of righteousness for me, so I may go in and thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.

L.19: Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will go in through them; I will give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.

R.19: Open the temple gates for me, the gates for people who do what is right! I will go in and thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.

decisions.choice: Open to me the gates: entering the temple
decisions.reason: The speaker asks to enter the temple courts, perhaps at the head of a procession. Psalms 15 and 24:3-10 also speak of who may enter and of gates opened.

decisions.choice: gates of righteousness: the gates through which the righteous enter
alternatives: the gates where justice is done
decisions.reason: Verse 20 explains the phrase: it is the LORD's gate, and the righteous go through it.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: the temple gates ... for people who do what is right
decisions.reason: Readable says which gates are meant (m1, m2).

records.source: זֶֽה־הַשַּׁ֥עַר לַיהוָ֑ה צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים יָבֹ֥אוּ בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: This [is] the gate of YHWH; [the] righteous will go in through it.
pieces: This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s gate; those who are righteous may pass through it.

L.20: This [is] the gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; [the] righteous will go in through it.

R.20: This is the gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house. People who do what is right will go in through it.

decisions.choice: This is the gate: perhaps the gatekeepers' answer
decisions.reason: The verse may be the reply of the priests or gatekeepers to the request of verse 19.

decisions.choice: the gate of the LORD's house
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the gate is the temple gate.

records.source: א֭וֹדְךָ כִּ֣י עֲנִיתָ֑נִי וַתְּהִי־לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: I will give thanks to you, for you have answered me and have become for me salvation.
pieces: I thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answered me and became my salvation.

L.21: I will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have answered me and have become my salvation.

R.21: I thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answered my prayer and saved me.

decisions.choice: you: thanks spoken to the LORD
decisions.reason: Inside the gates the speaker now speaks to the LORD directly, taking up the words of verse 14.

records.source: אֶ֭בֶן מָאֲס֣וּ הַבּוֹנִ֑ים הָ֝יְתָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ פִּנָּֽה׃
records.gloss: [A] stone [that] the builders rejected has become [the] head of [the] corner.
pieces: The stone the builders cast aside is now the stone at the head of the corner.

L.22: [The] stone the builders rejected has become [the] head of [the] corner.

R.22: The builders threw away a stone as useless, but it has become the most important stone in the building.

decisions.choice: head of the corner: the main stone of the building
decisions.reason: The phrase (rosh pinnah) is the chief stone at a corner: either the cornerstone of the foundation, which sets the line of the walls, or the top stone that completes them. Either way it is the most important stone.

decisions.choice: quoted of Jesus in the New Testament
decisions.reason: Jesus applies verses 22-23 to himself (Matthew 21:42; Mark 12:10-11; Luke 20:17), and Peter does the same (Acts 4:11; 1 Peter 2:7). In the psalm the rejected stone is the one the LORD rescued and honored, whether the king or Israel.

decisions.choice: the most important stone in the building
decisions.reason: Readable gives the point of the picture (m1).

records.source: מֵאֵ֣ת יְ֭הוָה הָ֣יְתָה זֹּ֑את הִ֖יא נִפְלָ֣את בְּעֵינֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: From YHWH this has come; it [is] wonderful in our eyes.
pieces: This has come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; we look on it with wonder.

L.23: From {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} this has come; it [is] wonderful in our eyes.

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did this, and it amazes us!

decisions.choice: quoted with verse 22
decisions.reason: Matthew 21:42 and Mark 12:11 quote this verse with verse 22.

decisions.choice: wonderful: beyond what anyone could do
decisions.reason: The word (nifla't) is used of the LORD's wonders (111:4): a thing only he could do.

records.source: זֶה־הַ֭יּוֹם עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה נָגִ֖ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָ֣ה בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: This [is] the day [that] YHWH has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.
pieces: This is the day on which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has acted; let us celebrate and be glad because of it.

L.24: This [is] the day [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.

R.24: Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this great thing! Let us celebrate and be happy about it.

decisions.choice: made: acted, brought about
decisions.reason: The verb ('asah) is to make or do. In this setting the day is the one on which the LORD has acted to save, the day of the festival that celebrates it.

decisions.choice: in it: in the day
decisions.reason: "It" (bo) is most likely the day; the same word could mean "in him", the LORD.

decisions.choice: acted (B); done this great thing (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the likely sense (m1).

records.source: אָנָּ֣א יְ֭הוָה הוֹשִׁ֘יעָ֥ה נָּ֑א אָֽנָּ֥א יְ֝הוָ֗ה הַצְלִ֘יחָ֥ה נָּֽא׃
records.gloss: Please, YHWH, save, please! Please, YHWH, give success, please!
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, save us! {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, give us success!

L.25: Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save, please! Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, give success, please!

R.25: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please save us! {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please help us do well!

decisions.choice: save, please: Hosanna
decisions.reason: The words "save, please" (hoshi'ah na') are the source of "Hosanna", which the crowds shouted as Jesus entered Jerusalem (Matthew 21:9; Mark 11:9; John 12:13).

decisions.choice: give success: make the way prosper
decisions.reason: The verb (hatslichah) is to make something go well or succeed (1:3; 45:5).

decisions.choice: us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the object of "save" and "give success".

records.source: בָּר֣וּךְ הַ֭בָּא בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בֵּ֝רַֽכְנוּכֶ֗ם מִבֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Blessed [is] the one who comes in [the] name of YHWH; we bless you from [the] house of YHWH.
pieces: Blessings on the one who comes in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s name! Out of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house we speak a blessing over you.

L.26: Blessed [is] the one who comes in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; we bless you from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.26: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless the one who comes in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name! From the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} we bless all of you.

decisions.choice: the one who comes ... you: the king or pilgrim, then all the worshipers
decisions.reason: The priests welcome the one who comes in the LORD's name, probably the king at the head of the procession, and then bless all who come with him ("you" is plural).

decisions.choice: sung when Jesus entered Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The crowds greeted Jesus with this line (Matthew 21:9; Mark 11:9; Luke 19:38; John 12:13), and Jesus said Jerusalem would not see him again until it said these words (Matthew 23:39; Luke 13:35).

decisions.choice: we bless you from the house of the LORD: the priests' blessing
decisions.reason: Blessing the people in the LORD's name was the work of the priests (Numbers 6:23-27).

decisions.choice: May the LORD bless
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who gives the blessing, which the Hebrew implies.

records.source: אֵ֤ל׀יְהוָה֮ וַיָּ֪אֶר לָ֥נוּ אִסְרוּ־חַ֥ג בַּעֲבֹתִ֑ים עַד־קַ֝רְנ֗וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: God [is] YHWH, and he has given light to us; bind [the] festival sacrifice with cords up to [the] horns of the altar.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is God; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us light. Tie the festival offering with ropes and bring it right to the altar's horns.

L.27: God [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us light; bind the festival sacrifice with cords up to the horns of the altar.

R.27: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has blessed us with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light. Tie up the animal for the festival sacrifice and bring it to the corners of the altar.

decisions.choice: he has given us light: he has shown us favor
decisions.reason: God's light shining on his people is his favor and help (4:7; Numbers 6:25).

decisions.choice: festival sacrifice ... cords
alternatives: join the festival procession with branches
decisions.reason: The word (chag) is a festival, and also the animal offered at it (Exodus 23:18). The word ('avotim) is ropes, but some take it as leafy branches carried in a procession up to the altar, as at the Festival of Booths. The renderings follow the more usual senses.

decisions.choice: the horns of the altar: its four corners
decisions.reason: The altar had a raised "horn" at each corner (Exodus 27:2). Blood from sacrifices was put on them (Leviticus 4:7).

records.source: אֵלִ֣י אַתָּ֣ה וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אֲרוֹמְמֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: My God [are] you, and I will give thanks to you; my God, I will exalt you.
pieces: You are my God, so I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; I will exalt {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my God.

L.28: My God [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and I will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; my God, I will exalt {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.28: You are my God, so I thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. My God, I will tell everyone how great {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are!

decisions.choice: echo of Exodus 15:2
decisions.reason: The line echoes the Song of the Sea again (as verse 14): "This is my God, and I will praise him ... and I will exalt him" (Exodus 15:2).

decisions.choice: exalt: lift high in praise
decisions.reason: The verb (romem) is to make high: to honor God as supreme (30:2; 34:4).

records.source: הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Give thanks to YHWH, for [he is] good; for forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever.

L.29: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever.

R.29: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good! His faithful love lasts forever.

decisions.choice: the psalm ends as it began
decisions.reason: The closing verse repeats verse 1 word for word, framing the whole psalm with thanks.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 118:1.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
